title: China Orders Removal of Windows 10 from State Agencies, Reports Say
description: Recent reports indicate that China is accelerating the removal of Microsoft Windows 10 from government computers due to security concerns.

sources.title: China Axing Microsoft Windows From State Agencies Ahead of Plan
China reportedly orders state agencies to uninstall its government-only edition of Windows 10 — Beijing accelerates planned retirement over data security concerns
EXCLUSIVE: Microsoft retreats in China, but AI boom helps it keep a window open

sections.heading: Government Directive
paragraphs: According to Tom's Hardware, China has reportedly ordered state agencies to uninstall its government-only edition of Windows 10. The source states that Beijing is accelerating a planned retirement over data security concerns.

sections.heading: Strategic Shift
paragraphs: Bloomberg.com reports that China is axing Microsoft Windows from state agencies. This action is reportedly occurring ahead of a previously outlined plan.

sections.heading: Microsoft's Market Status
paragraphs: According to Reuters, Microsoft is retreating in China. However, the report notes that the AI boom is helping the company keep a window open in the region.

sections.heading: Search Trend Context
paragraphs: The term 'windows 10' is currently trending in the US with a Google reported search lower bound of 100. Google Trends data highlights topics with significant spikes in search interest.

faq.q: Which version of Windows is affected?
faq.a: Tom's Hardware reports that the order specifically targets the government-only edition of Windows 10.

faq.q: How is Microsoft responding to the situation in China?
faq.a: According to Reuters, Microsoft is retreating in China, though the AI boom is reportedly helping it maintain a presence.
